1.summary: Marks all generated code so that coverage tools skip it. (Coverage is how much of your code the tests run.) The mark also lands on a class that users write part of themselves.

sections.title: Why
sections.text: Generated code is hard to test. It drags the coverage number down.

sections.title: Before → after
sections.text: Before: generated code counts in coverage. After: it is marked `[ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]` and skipped. Older project types do not get the mark.

sections.title: Must preserve
sections.text: Projects that build today must still build. Generated code must work the same.

sections.title: Approach
sections.text: All 6 code templates add the mark. One shared helper, `EmitNestingTypesAndNamespaces()`, also adds a line break.

sections.title: Alternatives
sections.text: The request mentions an on/off setting. None was added.

sections.title: Checks run
sections.text: Unit tests (`dotnet test`, a saved run on one machine, not the automatic server run): 169 of 169 pass. The new unit test only looks for the mark once per file. It ignores build errors.

sections.title: Open gaps
sections.text: If a user already added the same mark to their own class, it is there twice. That can break the build.
